thread:
support-bot: Alert: customer acme-inc reported p99 latency spike on /v1/generate (region: us-west1). See ticket #C-9182 :rotating_light:
alex: getting the ticket now, they say spike started ~04:10 UTC and coincides with auth 401/429s?
maya: hey – I can see a burst of retries in the request log around that time, lots of small payloads (avg tokens=12) + auth refresh failures from their app.
kevin: small payloads + continuous batcher = long hold windows while waiting for a cohort, that can blow up tail p99. if auth fails we get retries which increases arrival jitter.
sre_oncall: logs -- tail of runtime logs (filtered for acme):
```
2026-02-14T04:09:59Z INFO request id=rid_123 token_refresh=failed code=401
2026-02-14T04:10:01Z WARN batcher hold=200ms size=1 cohort=smallprompts
2026-02-14T04:10:02Z INFO request id=rid_124 retry=1
2026-02-14T04:10:05Z ERROR serve latency_ms=1420 p99
```
alex: interesting — our batcher config for smallprompts has hold_window=200ms and min_batch=2 on that fleet. when arrivals are jittery, single small requests wait near the full hold window.
maya: billing-bot also flagged an auth token refresh rate limit for acme earlier at 04:08 (they were getting 429 from our KMS integration). could be cascading.
billing-bot: note: acme has high token rotation rate, exceeded refresh quota at 04:07–04:11. 429s originated from ksm-proxy cluster.
kevin: hypothesis: auth 401/429s caused client retries -> bursts of tiny requests -> continuous batcher hold waiting for a cohort -> increased tail p99. combo of three things.
sre_oncall: repro plan: 1) run canary adjusting smallprompts hold_window -> 50ms, 2) enable batching-disabled fallback for acme on the edge for 10m, 3) add temporary routing to dedicate them to a fleet with prefix-caching enabled.
alex: can we reproduce locally with synthetic replay? I can replay their trace (we have request IDs) against staging batcher config.
maya: yes. repro steps (short):
1) pull request log for rid_123..rid_140 from prod (s3://replay/acme/04-10-2026.json)
2) run `./replay --target staging --batcher-config smallprompts.hold_window=200`
3) observe p95/p99 in staging metrics
kevin: quick mitigation I pushed to canary: changed smallprompts.hold_window=60ms on 2 nodes (canary group). also added a rule to detect >10% 401 in 1m and temporarily disable batching for that tenant.
sre_oncall: canary metrics already look better for the replay: p99 dropped from ~1.4s -> 320ms for the synthetic burst.
billing-bot: recommend disabling token auto-rotate for acme while they debug client-side refresh (ops approved a 15m exception).
alex: ops, please confirm rollback plan if canary causes regressions.
sre_oncall: rollback is trivial via toggles: revert hold_window and disable the tenant-rule. I left a playbook in #runbooks.
maya: next steps: - contact acme support engineer with repro steps and recommend they handle auth 401s (backoff, reduce rotation) - schedule a config rollout to all fleets with smaller hold_window for tiny payloads (gradual canary) - add a telemetry alert for tenant-level 401 spike -> auto-shed batching
kevin: long-term: consider adaptive hold_window based on inter-arrival distribution or use micro-batcher that immediately flushes when payload tokens < threshold.
alex: filing follow-up: create postmortem draft and link to ticket C-9182, include metrics, canary results, and config diff. I'll also add the replay artifact.
sre_oncall: closing the immediate incident: canary mitigation stays for 30m, ops has contact with acme, billing exception granted. tagging this thread with incident=C-9182. :white_check_mark:
